messages:
maya: Hey @people-ops — urgent one. My partner has a specialist appointment tomorrow in Madrid and the clinic is asking for an insurance ID card or proof of coverage. We enrolled them but their dependent enrollment went through late and they haven't received a physical card. Is a digital card screenshot OK? What’s the fastest way to get a temporary ID or letter they’ll accept?

alex (People Ops): Short answer: digital PDF is usually fine, but clinics vary. We can get an expedited proof-of-coverage letter from the insurer or a temporary member ID. Two quick paths: 1) download the insurer's digital ID PDF from the insurer portal and email that to the clinic, or 2) we can request an expedited coverage letter on your behalf.

maya: Clinic specifically said they need "member ID and group number" on a document. I can show the member portal screenshot but worried about format. Also we're out of the country so physical card impossible.

samir: FWIW I had this for a spouse — showed the insurer's PDF printout on my phone and they accepted it. If they want an official letter, insurer can email a letter with member/group numbers within a few hours if you call.

alex (People Ops): Ok steps: 1) Try to pull the digital ID PDF: https://benefits.example.com -> Benefits -> Insurance -> View ID Card. Use the "Download PDF" button, that has both member ID and group number and a policyholder name. 2) If you can’t get PDF, open chat with insurer or call their international line and ask for an "expedited proof of coverage" emailed to you. 3) If you want us to request it, reply here with partner full name, DOB, and last 4 of SSN (we’ll DM for PII). We can escalate to our broker for faster turnaround.

maya: Thanks. Tried portal, it shows an image but no download button. I can take a screenshot but I don’t want to risk rejection. I’ll DM the info.

alex (People Ops): Cool. Also, sample email you can send to the clinic if they prefer something from you directly:

```
Subject: Proof of Insurance — [Partner Name] (Appt: [date])

Hi,
We are scheduled for an appointment on [date]. Please find attached a screenshot of the member digital ID from our insurer. Member ID: [member id]
Group Number: [group]
Policy Holder: [Your name]
If additional verification is needed, you can contact [Insurer Name] international support at +1-XXX-XXX-XXXX or request an expedited proof of coverage via their portal.
Thanks,
[Your name]
```

alex (People Ops): For claims later, keep copies of anything they bill you and get an itemized invoice with CPT codes if possible. If a claim gets submitted out-of-network, we can help with appeal steps and sample letters.

people-ops-bot: Enrollment docs and expedited proof request form: https://hr.example.com/dependents -> "Request expedited coverage letter" :link:

samir: One more tip — ask the clinic to accept a phone verification line. Some clinics will call the insurer’s number and confirm member details. Saved me once.

maya: DMing Alex now with DOB + last4. Appreciate the quick help :pray:

alex (People Ops): Got it. I’ll submit the request and post the insurer response here when it comes through. If insurer can’t email a letter fast enough we’ll use the broker to push. :thumbsup:
